mainEntity.name: Should I choose open-cell or closed-cell spray foam for a steel workshop retrofit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The choice comes down to climate severity, space limits, and your workshop activities. Open-cell foam expands rapidly, fills deep purlin cavities, and costs less per board foot, but it is air-permeable, absorbs moisture, and cannot act as a standalone vapor barrier on bare metal panels. Closed-cell foam cures into a dense, rigid barrier with a high R-value per inch (roughly R-6 to R-7). It adds structural racking strength to sheet metal, completely blocks air infiltration, and forms an impermeable moisture barrier, making it the superior choice for unconditioned metal buildings in high-heat desert and mountain regions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Closed-cell is usually best for metal buildings because it repels moisture, forms an impermeable vapor barrier directly against steel, and delivers higher R-value per inch.
